title: Injective module presheaves are acyclic on presheaf Čech nerves
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category, $R$ a presheaf of rings, and $M$ an injective module presheaf [def-sp-injective-resolutions, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For every map $f:P\to Q$ of presheaves of sets, the complex $\check C^\bullet(f,M_{ab})$ [def-sc-presheaf-cech-complex] has zero cohomology in all degrees $q>0$. The values of $R$, $M$, $P$, and $Q$ belong to the same universe, so the free $R$-module presheaves used in the proof belong to the category in which $M$ is injective. No covering or site pullback hypothesis is required.

source.place: Proof of Tag 03FC, using 03F5, 03AT, 03AS; presheaf nerve version from Hypercoverings 01GC

proof.text: Write q=n+1. Use positive exactness of the free module presheaf nerve K and the additive comparison e between Hom(K_i,M) and abelian Cech cochains.

For a cocycle c, its inverse under e is a map a:K_(n+1)->M killing K_(n+2)->K_(n+1), by boundary compatibility and injectivity of e. Apply Mathlib ShortComplex.Exact.descToInjective to the exact short complex K_(n+2)->K_(n+1)->K_n. The identity comp_descToInjective shows that its extension b:K_n->M pulls back to a. Boundary compatibility sends b to a cochain whose differential is c.
ShortComplex.ab_exact_iff converts this cocycle lifting into ExactAt of the abelian Cech complex at n+1. ExactAt.isZero_homology gives the asserted zero homology.
